examples.title: Worked application: Problem formulation and state-space search
steps: Represent a search problem using an initial state, available actions, a transition model, a goal test, and a path-cost function. practiceQuestions.prompt: In a route-finding problem, which specification is necessary to evaluate whether a route reaches the destination?

A list of variable names unrelated to the route

practiceQuestions.explanation: A search problem needs a goal test; route cost may also be required when the task is to minimise distance or time.

examples.title: Worked application: Heuristics and A*
steps: A heuristic h(n) estimates the remaining cost from state n to a goal. A* ranks nodes using f(n)=g(n)+h(n), where g(n) is cost already incurred. Under standard conditions, an admissible heuristic never overestimates the true remaining cost; consistency further constrains estimates across edges.
Identify the assumption or condition on which the explanation depends.
Apply the same principle to a changed case and state what would change in the result.
Write a conclusion that answers the question directly and notes one relevant limitation.
examples.note: Original Student Plug teaching example; not an official university solution or verified past examination question.

practiceQuestions.prompt: A* evaluates a node using which expression?
options: f(n)=g(n)+h(n)
f(n)=g(n)−h(n) only
f(n)=h(n) regardless of path cost
f(n)=number of nodes in memory
practiceQuestions.explanation: A* combines path cost already incurred with an estimate of remaining cost.
